messages:
emma: Heads-up — observed a regression where embedding requests are being accepted by route-scoped API keys that should only allow chat. Started after yesterday's RBAC/roles refactor deploy.

emma: Minimal reproduction in prod logs: server shows token scopes = ['chat:write'] but handled as embeddings call.

emma: Log snippet:
```
INFO auth: token_id=key_abc123 scopes=[chat:write] route=/v1/embeddings model=text-embedding-3 accepted=true
WARN handler: handled as embeddings request (model=text-embedding-3) despite token scopes mismatch
```

devon: Repro locally with curl using a scoped key: it returns 200 and embedding vector. curl:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-scoped-chat-only" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
returned 200 and vector payload.

raj: Possible root cause: our scope-check middleware was refactored. If the code does an "any(required_scope in token_scopes)" check for route groups, chat vs embeddings namespace overlap could let chat-only pass for embeddings. Can you paste the middleware snippet?

devon: Found it in auth/middleware.go — current logic (pseudocode):
```
// BAD: allows if any required scope matches
func checkScopes(tokenScopes, requiredScopes []string) bool {
  for _, rs := range requiredScopes {
    for _, ts := range tokenScopes {
      if strings.HasPrefix(ts, rs) {
        return true
      }
    }
  }
  return false
}
```

raj: Yeah that's the bug — should require ALL required scopes (or an appropriate superset). Fix: replace logic with `all(required in tokenScopes OR superset match)`. Also need to ensure prefix matching doesn't allow crossing namespaces (chat vs embeddings).

olivia: Also noticed audit logs for these requests are missing scope_denied events. We have requests flowing through without emitting an audit event when scope mismatch should happen. That will make forensics harder.

sec-bot: SECURITY_ALERT: potential over-permissive token enforcement detected. Risk: data exfil via embeddings with chat-only keys. Severity: high.

emma: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Hotfix the check to require all scopes and deploy, 2) Revert the RBAC refactor commit, 3) Short-term: deny embeddings routes for keys with `chat:`-only scopes at the API gateway (WAF rule). Which is fastest?

devon: Hotfix is small (change any->all) and tests. I can push a patch to a hotfix branch and run canary in us-east in ~30-45m. Revert is riskier since refactor included other fixes. Gateway rule could be faster but messy.

raj: Also: rotate any keys we think were impacted and issue a forced rotation as precaution. We should mark those keys compromised until rotated. KMS integration note: if we revoke via control plane we must ensure private deployments' synced KMS caches invalidate quickly — otherwise some on-prem pods might still accept old tokens until KMS cache TTL expires. Olivia, can you check cache TTLs?

olivia: Private deploys default cache TTL is 300s, but some customer configs increased it to 1800s. We need to push an invalidation message to the sync bus for all Private customers to expedite. I can script that.

sre-oncall: Will open a high-priority incident channel for tracking and paging. Also recommend increasing audit log verbosity for auth for the next 60m to capture full token scope payloads (PII-safe) for triage.

emma: Triage plan (short):
- devon: patch scope check (any -> all) + unit tests + deploy hotfix canary (ETA 45m)
- raj: prepare key rotation list, identify keys with `chat:` only that called embeddings in the last 24h (use access logs) + mark for rotation (ETA 1h)
- olivia: push KMS/cache invalidation to private deployments + increase auth audit verbosity for 1h (ETA 20m)
- emma: open incident, notify Legal/Compliance and CS for affected customers, prepare customer-facing template (ETA 30m)
- sec-bot: add automated monitor to alert if embeddings requests succeed with tokens not containing embeddings scope (instant)

devon: Hotfix PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/8172 — change is a one-line logic fix plus tests. Running CI now.

raj: Forensics query to run against logs (Elasticsearch):
```
index: auth-* | where route=="/v1/embeddings" and not token_scopes contains "embedding" | stats count by token_id
```
I'll run and dump top 100 token_ids.

olivia: I'm publishing a sync invalidation job to the sync bus: `syncctl invalidate-keys --all-customers --reason="rbac-fix-1781200000"` and enabling higher auth logs. Will post job id when done.

devon: Canary passed in us-east after hotfix; no regressions in latencies. Preparing prod deploy.

sre-oncall: Deploying hotfix to prod now. Will monitor for error budget and 5xxs.

emma: After deploy — confirm audit events appear for previous mismatches and we're seeing 403 for chat-only keys on embeddings.

olivia: Invalidation job done. Job id: syncjob_20240318_8421. Private nodes should drop old keys within TTL window; sent push to expedite.

raj: For key rotation: found 37 distinct token_ids used for embeddings with chat-only scopes in last 24h. Marked them in the control plane and queued rotation. I'll coordinate with Customer Success to rotate keys for customer-managed keys.

devon: Follow-up actions we should do before closing incident:
- Add e2e tests for per-route+per-model scope enforcement for chat vs embeddings
- Add unit tests for scope matching logic to prevent prefix cross-namespace matches
- Emit explicit audit event `scope_denied` with details (route, required_scopes, token_scopes) and ensure retention for 90d
- Backfill audit logs for last 24h where possible (run offline enrichment job)

emma: Agreed. I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates. Assigning owners in the incident ticket.

sec-bot: Incident severity lowered to "high -> mitigated" after hotfix deploy. Continue monitoring for 24h.

devon: PR merged, prod hotfix deployed, and tests added.

sre-oncall: No spikes in 5xxs, monitoring shows embeddings calls now return 403 for chat-only keys.

emma: Closing notes — required follow-ups:
- raj: complete forced rotations and coordinate with customers (48h)
- olivia: ensure sync invalidation is documented and add a bulk-invalidate endpoint (week)
- devon: add stronger scope matcher (exact namespace semantics) + fuzz tests (2 weeks)
- emma: postmortem write-up + customer comms (48h)

emma: Thanks everyone. Put any leftover items in the incident ticket and we'll review in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
